corrected_draft.title: DOJ Drops Proposed Divestiture of Google AI Investments
corrected_draft.description_short: On March 7, 2025, the Justice Department dropped a proposal to require Google to sell its AI investments while continuing to seek Chrome divestiture and other antitrust remedies.
corrected_draft.description_medium: On March 7, 2025, the Justice Department dropped its proposal to require Google to sell investments in AI companies, including Anthropic, in its search-monopoly case. Reuters reported that DOJ and 38 state attorneys general continued to seek Chrome divestiture and other remedies. The discrete change concerned one proposed remedy, not dismissal of the antitrust case.
corrected_draft.description_long: On March 7, 2025, the U.S. Department of Justice dropped a proposal to require Alphabet’s Google to sell its investments in artificial-intelligence companies, including Anthropic, as part of the search-monopoly litigation. Reuters reported that prosecutors said evidence gathered since an earlier draft raised a risk of unintended consequences in the evolving AI sector. DOJ instead sought prior notice of future generative-AI investments. The department and a coalition of 38 state attorneys general continued to seek a court order requiring Google to divest its Chrome browser and to adopt other remedies addressing the search monopoly. The change was therefore a withdrawal of one proposed remedy within an ongoing antitrust case. It was not a decision to abandon the litigation. A corrected entry should name the AI-investment remedy and the March filing while distinguishing it from the still-pending claims and proposed Chrome relief.

corrected_draft.title: Trump Revokes Federal Contractor Affirmative-Action Order
corrected_draft.description_short: On January 21, 2025, Trump revoked Executive Order 11246 and directed changes to federal contractor affirmative-action requirements, with a 90-day transition period.
corrected_draft.description_medium: On January 21, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14173, which revoked Executive Order 11246 and directed the Labor Department’s contractor-compliance office to cease promoting diversity and holding contractors responsible for affirmative action. The order allowed contractors to continue following the prior regulatory scheme for 90 days. It was signed January 21, not January 20.
corrected_draft.description_long: On January 21, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14173, “Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity.” The order revoked Executive Order 11246, which had governed equal employment opportunity requirements for federal contractors. It directed the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs to cease promoting diversity and holding federal contractors and subcontractors responsible for affirmative action. The order also required federal contracts and grants to include terms concerning compliance with federal anti-discrimination laws and certifications about unlawful DEI programs. For 90 days, contractors could continue complying with the regulatory scheme that had been in effect on January 20. The title should therefore identify the January 21 order and its contractor provisions rather than claim that every contracting requirement ended on January 20. The White House text is primary evidence of the order’s date and terms; broader implementation effects are outside this event description.

corrected_draft.title: Trump Removes Two EEOC Commissioners and the General Counsel
corrected_draft.description_short: On January 27, 2025, Trump removed EEOC Commissioners Charlotte Burrows and Jocelyn Samuels and General Counsel Karla Gilbride.
corrected_draft.description_medium: On January 27, 2025, President Donald Trump removed Equal Employment Opportunity Commission members Charlotte Burrows and Jocelyn Samuels and the agency’s general counsel, Karla Gilbride. Reuters reported that the five-member commission already had one vacancy; removing the two commissioners left it without the three members needed for a quorum. The event was not the firing of three of five commissioners on January 20.
corrected_draft.description_long: On January 27, 2025, President Donald Trump removed two Democratic members of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, Commissioners Charlotte Burrows and Jocelyn Samuels, and fired the agency’s general counsel, Karla Gilbride. Reuters reported that the EEOC was an independent five-member commission with staggered terms and already had one vacancy. Removing Burrows and Samuels left the remaining members without the quorum of three needed to adopt rules and guidance, direct some staff actions, and issue rulings in federal-employee discrimination cases. The removal of commissioners was described as unprecedented by Reuters, which also reported that the former commissioners were considering legal action. This supports a specific January 27 personnel action involving two commissioners and the general counsel. It does not support a claim that Trump fired three commissioners on January 20. The corrected title and description should preserve the exact count, roles and date.
